evidence: Only one top-level package ('core') with flat module structure (no sub-packages)
Main.py directly imports and orchestrates core modules without clear separation of concerns

All core modules (User_Functions, Checks, InsertData, Other) contain procedural functions with cross-cutting dependencies (e.g., InsertData imports core.Checks, User_Functions imports mysql.connector directly)
No evidence of inversion of control, dependency injection, or clear architectural boundaries (e.g., no adapters/ports, no controllers/services separation)
High cohesive coupling to infrastructure (direct mysql.connector usage across modules)
Minimal abstraction layers - modules are grouped by functionality but not by architectural layering
Repository depth of only 2 levels indicates flat organization typical of scripts or small monolithic applications
risks: Tight coupling between business logic and infrastructure (database access scattered across modules)
Difficult to test components in isolation due to missing abstractions and direct dependencies
Scalability limitations due to monolithic structure without explicit boundaries
High maintenance cost as changes in one area (e.g., database) ripple across modules
Lack of clear separation between application core and external concerns
